rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something becoming worse or going bad without emphasizing a specific type of decay.

example.english: This fish has been left for two days and is starting to decay.
example.traditional: 呢啲魚擺咗兩日，開始變壞喇。
example.jyutping: ni1 di1 jyu4 baai2 zo2 loeng5 jat6 hoi1 ci2 bin3 waai6 laa3

rows.note: Use this for a decline in quality, condition, performance, or health rather than physical rotting.

example.english: My memory has started to decay lately.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zeoi3 gan6 gei3 jik1 lik6 bin3 caa1 zo2

rows.note: Use this instead of 變壞 when food, a body, or another organic material is physically rotting.

example.english: The apple has started to decay from being left out.
example.jyutping: go3 ping4 gwo2 baai2 dou3 fu6 laan6 laa3

rows.note: Use this causative pattern when something makes another thing rot or deteriorate.

example.english: Dampness can cause wood to decay.
example.jyutping: ciu4 sap1 wui5 ling6 muk6 tau4 bin3 waai6
